sections.h2: City of Fairfax versus Fairfax County
sections.html:
The City of Fairfax is a compact independent city of about 6.3 square miles, 14 miles west of Washington, D.C. It is the county seat, yet it governs itself apart from Fairfax County. The county surrounds it, and a small county exclave inside the city limits holds the courthouse complex and the jail.

Check your tax bill to learn who sends it. A Fairfax mailing address can belong to a house in the city or in the county, and each has its own assessors, tax office and school arrangements.

Population was 24,146 in 2020 and is estimated at 26,772 for 2025, about 10.9 percent higher. The 2020 count showed 9,330 housing units with 5.7 percent vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.7 percent, so owned houses rarely sit empty, and a neglected one stands out to neighbors and code staff. Absentee owners often decide to sell fast for that reason.

Fairfax began as the Town of Providence in 1805, grew around the courthouse, incorporated as a town in 1874 and became an independent city in 1961. The City of Fairfax Historic District was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1987. If your house is in or near the old town, ask the planning office whether any exterior work you did needed city approval before you list.

City government is the largest employer inside the limits, with 600 employees, followed by firms such as Sentry Force, Zeta Associates and Ted Britt Ford with 250 to 499 each. George Mason University, with 33,917 students, sits just south of the city line with a small part of its grounds inside it. Many residents work at the university, in Tysons or in Washington, and owners reassigned to a new post may need to sell quickly. A cash sale can be timed around a move.

sections.h2: How the city assesses real estate
sections.html:
Every property is assessed each year at 100 percent of fair market value, effective January 1. The assessor does not set the rate. City Council sets it during the budget process, and the rate multiplied by your assessment produces the bill. For houses, the assessor prefers the market data approach, which compares recent sales of similar homes in the same neighborhood.

Assessment stepTypical timing
Effective date of assessmentJanuary 1
Assessment notices mailedLate February
Administrative review requestWithin 30 days of notices, around early April
Tax bills mailedMid May
Appeal to Board of EqualizationJune 30

City taxes are paid on June 21 and December 5. The Treasurer's number is 703-385-7900, and the city offers tax relief for the elderly and disabled.

Begin with the Real Estate Assessment Office at City Hall. Owners have 30 days after notices go out to ask for a review by phone or in person, and an appraiser can go over the data and schedule an inspection. If that does not settle it, the next stop is the Board of Equalization.

The board has three members, appointed by the Circuit Court from among city property owners. It can affirm, reduce or raise an assessment to even out the tax burden, and a disagreement with the board can go on to Circuit Court.

  • Collect recent comparable sales and photos of condition problems.
  • Submit the city's administrative appeal form before the review deadline.
  • Keep repair estimates if you think the assessor missed damage.

U.S. 50 and U.S. 29 meet in the northeast corner and share Fairfax Boulevard for about 2.8 miles through the city. State Routes 123, 236 and 237 also cross it, and Interstate 66 runs just outside the limits, reached by U.S. 50 or Route 123. The Vienna Metro station on the Orange Line and the Burke Centre station for Virginia Railway Express and Amtrak are outside the city, and the city runs its own CUE Bus.

Blenheim Boulevard work is scheduled to wrap up in July 2028, so owners on or near that road may see construction while the house is listed.

A seller clears any unpaid city real estate tax from the sale proceeds and pays Virginia's grantor tax, which is 50 cents per $500 of the price and normally the seller's. Tax liens take priority over other liens, and the contract decides how tax is prorated between buyer and seller. Deeds are recorded with the land records office at the Fairfax County Judicial Center.

  • Ask the Treasurer for the amount due before the closing date.
  • Check the settlement statement for the grantor tax line.
  • Confirm how recording costs are split in the contract.

sections.h2: What to prepare before you list or sell
sections.html:
Owners in the city get the best result by starting with the paperwork. Find the most recent assessment notice, your tax bill and any permits for additions, decks or roofing. Then ask yourself honestly where the house looks tired: a worn kitchen, an aging furnace, a damp basement. Buyers and inspectors find these things, and a seller who names them first keeps control of the conversation.

If the house is empty, neighbors and code staff will notice sooner than in a larger place, so keep the yard cut and the mail cleared. For an estate sale, confirm who may sign the deed and have that person ready to meet the title company.

After you accept an offer, the title company searches the record, orders payoffs for any tax or lien, and prepares the deed. You sign, the funds move, and the deed goes to the land records office. Because no lender is involved in a cash purchase, the date depends on how fast the title work clears and on when you want to move. Tell us your timeline at the start, whether that is a short window for a new assignment or a longer one while you find your next home.

sections.h2: Selling for cash in the city
sections.html:
A cash sale skips listing prep, repairs and showings. You describe the house, we make an offer based on its condition and title, and you decide. We buy directly or bring a vetted cash buyer. If you want to compare it with an agent listing, ask for our offer first and then weigh the two.

Before you talk to anyone, gather your latest assessment notice, tax bill and any permits for past work. If you think the assessment is too high, start the review process, since it can change your tax bill whether or not you sell. The title company will handle payoffs and the deed once you accept.

faqs.q: Is the City of Fairfax the same as Fairfax County?
faqs.a: No. The city sits inside the county but runs its own government, assessments and tax billing, and it remains the county seat.

faqs.q: When are City of Fairfax real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are paid on June 21 and December 5. Call the Treasurer at 703-385-7900 for your current bill and any balance before closing.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Fairfax city assessment?
faqs.a: You have 30 days after notices go out to request an administrative review, and the Board of Equalization appeal is due June 30. Dates shift each year, so check the assessments page.

faqs.q: Does the seller pay a tax when a Virginia house sells?
faqs.a: Yes. Virginia charges a grantor tax of 50 cents per $500 of the price, and the seller usually pays, although the contract can assign it differently.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Fairfax house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can take it in its current condition, and you pick the closing date. A title company still handles the deed and any payoffs.
